original_test_intent: Verify one-shot implicit correctable DRAM injection for each required physical slot, proving that the approved target generates exactly one attributable CE on the defined trigger and then automatically stops injecting.
original_method: Map every required slot to socket/die/UMC and any channel/rank selector supported by the tool; select one BIOS profile; capture baseline counters; arm mode 0 on one approved tuple; perform the exact documented memory access that consumes the injection; show one counter/event delta at the mapped slot; repeat the trigger to prove no second injection; disarm/inspect residual state, verify memory health and restore configuration before another target.
manual_activity: The FAE maps tuple to physical slot, defines the consuming memory access, arms one-shot mode, supervises exactly one trigger and proves disarm, then restores tool/HDT/BIOS state.
required_inputs: Populated slot to socket/die/UMC/channel/rank map and required target list
Reason for or replacement of hardcoded tuple 0:0:3
AMD tool/spec version/hash/license and errormode 0/setinjectionmode 0/mcapolling 0/errortype 0 semantics
Exact memory access that triggers the implicit event and target address/allocation
Evidence for arm, one CE consumption, no second event and disarm
DRAM-versus-MCA profile, timeout, abort, recovery and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated ECC SUT and controlled synthetic memory access
Verify tuple maps to intended slot; never iterate tuples by numeric guess
Capture counters before arm and after first/second trigger to detect residual injection
Stop on wrong slot, multiple events, UCE escalation, reset, poison or memory degradation
No automatic retry; explicitly verify/disarm injector and restore settings
agent_execution_scope: Validate topology, package semantics, trigger, profile and one-shot evidence plan
Collect read-only counters, transcript, OS/BMC event and post-health evidence
Do not choose tuple/trigger, alter BIOS/HDT, arm/inject, repeat automatically, recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve per-slot tuple coverage and trigger
Approve profile/package/timeout and one controlled execution
Verify disarm, restore and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Broad log filtering cannot establish that mode 0 injected once, identify the trigger or show automatic disarm.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Arm setinjectionmode 0 on one mapped tuple, perform one approved synthetic access, compare exact counter/event deltas, then perform a non-destructive verification access proving no second event.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: errormode 0, tuple 0:0:3, setinjectionmode 0, mcapolling 0, errortype 0, both profiles, slots 1~N and 60/60 minutes are preserved; target/trigger gaps remain explicit.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use per-slot tuple mapping and counter deltas to prove arm, exactly one triggered CE and automatic disarm for each separately approved target.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds trigger identity, single-consumption proof, negative second-access check, complete topology and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A tool PASS or one generic CE cannot prove one-shot semantics or Memory slot 1~N coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An unresolved tuple or trigger can hit the wrong DIMM; failure to disarm can turn one-shot coverage into repeated fault injection.

project_override_considerations: If tuple 0:0:3 is merely an example, replace it per the approved topology at execution time. If the tool cannot select channel/rank, define how multiple physical slots behind one UMC are distinguished or narrow coverage through engineering approval.
expected_evidence: Pre-arm status/counters and full arm command
Approved trigger transcript plus exactly one attributed CE delta
Second verification access with no additional injection and explicit disarm status
Memory health, restoration and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Memory slot 1~N is represented by only socket/die/UMC 0:0:3 with no channel/rank iteration. The implicit trigger is absent, so one-shot consumption/disarm cannot be tested. Two BIOS profiles conflict, timeout is undefined and Windows conflicts with dmesg.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The one-shot implicit CE purpose and literal mode are clear. Engineering can supply topology and trigger semantics, so static review completes while execution is gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 49 Wistron-System RAS-00769-V003: provide slot-to-socket/die/UMC/channel/rank coverage and approve/correct tuple 0:0:3; define the exact memory access that consumes the implicit one-shot plus arm, exactly-one-event, negative second-trigger and disarm evidence; decide DRAM-versus-MCA profile; approve AMD tool/spec provenance and mode flags, Linux/Windows/BMC oracle, timeout, aborts, recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Makes one-shot behavior observable as arm-to-single-consume-to-disarm rather than accepting a generic corrected event, while exposing the missing physical-slot iteration.
independent_technical_reasoning: `setinjectionmode 0` is meaningful only if the test demonstrates what arms the injector, what access consumes it and that a second access does not create another event. A socket/die/UMC tuple may cover several channels or DIMMs, so it cannot by itself substantiate slot 1~N. Tool PASS can occur at arm time before any DRAM access, making counter and event deltas around the trigger essential.
